1940年12月21日。晨间译稿。

《诚言报》、《新闻报》、《申报》、《国民导报》、
《中美日报》：

日军卡车坠入苏州河

据华光社发布之消息，12月19日夜，一辆日军军用卡车在闸北中山路经过中山桥时，因司机疏忽大意，坠入苏州河。致使六七名日本士兵溺亡，许多重物沉入河中。
逃脱者向附近日军司令部报告后，大批日军官兵赶赴现场视察，并试图从水中打捞遇难者尸体及物品。
鉴于此次事故可能系中国游击队所为，事发地点附近立即实施戒严，中山路交通被切断。行人受到严格搜查。

《诚言报》（评论）：

12月18日晚，一辆日军军用卡车违反交通规则，在南京路与四川路路口与一辆公共汽车相撞，导致数名日本士兵受伤，其中一人伤势危重。
12月19日，一辆日军军用卡车高速通过中山桥时，坠入苏州河，淹死六七名日本士兵。
车辆四处鲁莽疾驰，极易引发事故。然而，肇事者对此置若罔闻，肆意妄为。

《诚言报》、《中美日报》、《新闻报》、
《申报》、《国民导报》：

雇佣警察击伤行人

昨日凌晨1时54分，一名“市警”在西区罗便臣路（Robison Road）与彭宁路（Penging Road）路口开枪击伤一名行人。
枪击发生后，该警察逃逸。事件起因不明。

《诚言报》（评论）：

page_data.en:
December 22, 1940. Morning Translation.

Cheng Yien Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, Shun Pao, National Herald, Sin Wan Pao :-

CONDITIONS IN THE WESTERN DISTRICT

The Japanese authorities in the Western District are undertaking the construction of a Sasaki Road from the middle part of Great Western Road leading to Yi Yuen Road to commemorate the Japanese gendarme Sasaki who were murdered three weeks ago in Lane 5C on Great Western Road. As a result, about 300 more Chinese people were rendered homeless on December 21. A small number of houses at Wang Ka Loong (王家弄) were demolished yesterday. Residents in the lane are moving out.

Conditions in the Western District remained the same yesterday. In the blockaded areas on Great Western Road, south of Edinburgh Road, and at the intersection of Great Western Road and Bubbling Well Road, traffic was still blocked. Barbed wire barricades are to be seen everywhere at Tza Ka Lu, but the district was not blockaded. The S.M.P. adopted precautionary measures on the Settlement borders in the Western District and pedestrians and vehicles were searched at the intersections of Avenue Foch and Avenue Haig, of Bubbling Well Road and Avenue Haig, of Avenue Road and Jessfield Road and of Kiaochoo Road and Singapore Road, lest undesirable elements should enter the Settlement.

Large and small gambling dens and Jwo Hwei Lottery agents are to be found in operation in nearly every alleyway along Great Western Road and Edinburgh Road, south of Avenue Haig.

Cheng Yien Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, Sin Wan Pao, National Herald, Shun Pao :-

BARBED WIRE BARRICADES PLACED AT TU SAN WEI

On December 21, the Japanese erected barbed wire barricades at Tu San Wei (土山湾), Zikawei, and searched pedestrians. The Japanese regarded certain daily necessaries as prohibited articles and for this reason, many dealers were detained by Japanese gendarmes. Many shops at Tu San Wei, which sold the above "prohibited articles" to dealers were sealed by the Japanese.
page_data.zh:
1940年12月22日。晨间译稿。

《诚言报》、《中美日报》、《申报》、《国民新闻》、《新晚报》：

西区状况

日本当局在西区正着手修建一条佐佐木路（Sasaki Road），该路由大西路（Great Western Road）中段通往忆园路（Yi Yuen Road），以纪念三周前在大西路5C弄被杀害的日本宪兵佐佐木。因此，12月21日又有约300名中国人无家可归。昨日，王家弄（Wang Ka Loong）的少量房屋被拆除。该弄堂的居民正在搬离。

昨日西区状况依旧。在大西路爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）以南路段，以及大西路与静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）交汇处，交通仍然受阻。在曹家渡（Tza Ka Lu）随处可见铁丝网路障，但该区域并未被封锁。工部局警务处（S.M.P.）在西区租界边界采取了预防措施，并在福煦路与海格路、静安寺路与海格路、爱文义路与极司菲尔路、胶州路与新加坡路的交叉路口对行人和车辆进行检查，以防不良分子进入租界。

在海格路以南的大西路和爱丁堡路沿线的几乎每条小巷里，都有大小赌档以及“聚惠”彩票（Jwo Hwei Lottery）代理点在运营。

《诚言报》、《中美日报》、《新晚报》、《国民新闻》、《申报》：

土山湾设置铁丝网路障

12月21日，日本人在土山湾（Tu San Wei）、徐家汇（Zikawei）设立铁丝网路障，并搜查行人。日本人将某些日常必需品视为违禁品，因此许多商贩被日本宪兵拘留。土山湾许多向商贩出售上述“违禁品”的商店被日本人查封。

page_data.en:
December 22, 1940. Morning Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News, National Herald, Cheng Yien Pao,
Sin Wan Pao and Shun Pao :-

SHANGHAI MAYOR TO ESTABLISH INDEPENDENT TAX COLLECTING
OFFICE

In connection with the establishment of
a tax collecting office in the extra-Settlement roads area,
Mayor Chen Kung-po yesterday made a statement to the effect
that, as is done in the case of co-operation in the
functioning of police rights with the Settlement authorities,
the tax collecting office will also be placed under joint
control by the Settlement and the City Government authorities,
but it must be governed by the latter while the funds to be
collected therefrom will be used to meet the expenses in
the maintenance of co-operation in the functioning of police
rights as well as to cover other expenses in the extra-
Settlement roads area. In the event of the revenue being
found to be insufficient to cover the expenses, the
deficiency will be made up by the City Government and in
case there is a balance it will be spent on the development
of the extra-Settlement roads.

Chinese-American Daily News, Cheng Yien Pao, National Herald,
Shun Pao and Sin Wan Pao :-

December 23, 1940. Morning Translation

Cheng Yien Pao, National Herald, Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao :-

DEMOLITION OF HOUSES IN WANG KA LOONG STILL IN PROGRESS

Yesterday the demolition of houses in Wang Ka Loong (王家弄) off Great Western Road in the Western District was under way following the announcement by the Japanese of their intention to widen the alleyway into "Sasage Road." Most of the houses have been pulled down and only several houses at the end of the alleyway are remaining, but the inmates of these houses, about 200 in number, have received notices to leave the premises not later than December 25.

The conditions in the Western District remained as usual yesterday. The barbed wire barricades at the intersection of Great Western Road and Bubbling Well Road were still in evidence, while a state of semi-blockade prevailed on various street intersections leading to the Jessfield Village. The exit at the junction of Avenue Road and Jessfield Road had been enlarged, but the No.7 Route buses of the China General Omnibus Company had not resumed their usual route of operation. The No.14 Route buses still did not go beyond Bubbling Well Road and Avenue Haig.

The time of opening at Chu An Pang (诸安浜) and Yung Yuen Pang (永源浜) off Edinburgh Road, which were re-opened on December 20, was extended yesterday to 8 p.m., but the mercenary policemen on duty there strictly prohibited the residents from removing things out of the area.

Cheng Yien Pao (comment) :-

Demolition of people's houses

"Military officers" have been repeatedly attacked in districts under their control. Exasperated, they start to demolish the houses in Wang Ka Loong and the reason given by them for such a step is that they are going to construct Sasage Road in memory of the military officer named Sasage who had been killed.

In reality, they are venting their anger at the expense of the innocent people. In the meantime, it shows why the "prominent characters," who "take upon themselves the task of rescuing the people from the catastrophe," are powerless in the case of the residents in Wang Ka Loong who are being rendered homeless.

《诚言报》、《国民新闻报》、《申报》、《新闻报》：

西区王家弄拆屋仍在进行中

昨日，继日本人宣布拟将小巷拓宽为“佐佐木路”（Sasage Road）之后，西区大西路（Great Western Road）旁王家弄的拆屋工作随即展开。大部分房屋已被拆除，仅剩巷尾的几幢房屋，但这些房屋的住户约200人已接到通知，须于12月25日前搬离。

昨日西区情形如常。大西路与静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）交叉口的铁丝网路障依然可见，通往极司菲尔村（Jessfield Village）的各街道交叉口仍处于半封锁状态。爱文义路（Avenue Road）与极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）交界处的出口已扩大，但中国公共汽车公司的7路公共汽车尚未恢复原有行驶路线。14路公共汽车仍不越过静安寺路与海格路（Avenue Haig）。

爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）旁的诸安浜和永源浜已于12月20日重新开放，昨日其开放时间延长至晚上8时，但在该处执勤的雇佣警察严禁居民将物品搬出该区域。

《诚言报》（评论）：

拆毁民房

“军官”在其控制区内屡遭袭击。恼羞成怒之下，他们开始拆毁王家弄的房屋，并称此举是为了修建佐佐木路，以纪念被杀的名为佐佐木的军官。

实际上，他们是在拿无辜百姓泄愤。与此同时，这也说明了那些“自命承担拯救民众于水火之重任”的“显要人物”，在王家弄居民流离失所一事上为何无能为力。

page_data.en:
National Herald (comment) :-
THE RESULT OF THE NEW ORDER
In the eyes of a certain party, the Western
District is Wang's property. The tenants of the 300 houses
in Wang Ka Loong were ejected yesterday and more than 1,000
persons were rendered homeless and have to suffer hunger and
cold. This is one result of the new order; it tells us who
are the persons responsible for the homeless conditions of
these people.
Certain persons have shamelessly said: "Every
one who is warm-blooded loves his country, while all who have
a conscience love their fellow countrymen. Consequently, no
one can remain patient or indifferent or adopt a wait-and-see
attitude when he observes his country is on the verge of
collapse and his fellow countrymen in a very distressing
state."
This is a statement intended only to deceive
the people.
page_data.zh:
《国民导报》（评论）：
新秩序之结果
在某党人士眼中，西区乃汪氏之私产。昨日，王家弄三百户租户被逐，致使千余人无家可归，饱受饥寒之苦。此即新秩序之结果之一；它向我们揭示了谁应对这些人的流离失所负责。
某些人厚颜无耻地声称：“凡有血气者皆爱国，凡有良心者皆爱同胞。因此，当目睹国家濒临崩溃、同胞处于极度困苦之境时，无人能保持耐心、冷漠或采取观望态度。”
此言纯属欺世盗名之举。

Chinese-American Daily News, Cheng Yien Pao, Sin Wan Pao,
Shun Pao, National Herald :-

CONDITIONS IN THE WESTERN DISTRICT

The situation in the Western District
yesterday was easier. Some of the barricades placed
on Yu Yuen Road and Bubbling Well Road were removed, much
to the convenience of vehicles. The number of Japanese
soldiers and mercenary policemen on duty was the same.
Pedestrians were still being searched. Passage was
allowed on Yoo Ping Road and the barbed wire barricades
were still in position in the middle of the road, where
some mercenary policemen were stationed.

P. T. O.

Restrictions were still in force yesterday
on the passage at Chu An Pang (诸安浜), Edinburgh Road.
Most of the residents living in this lane moved out yesterday.
Some 300 mud huts at Tang Ka Tsung (汤家村)
in Tang Ka Loong (汤家弄), Great Western Road, were
demolished, rendering homeless some 1,000 persons. Yesterday,
poor people moved out from the lane. Strict restrictions
were placed on the dispatch of foodstuffs into the lane,
and even small quantities of vegetables and rice were
prohibited.

Cheng Yien Pao (comment) :-

"DO YOU AGREE?"

About a month ago the Japanese "resolved to
close" the gambling dens in the Badlands. The gambling
dens did not cease their operations but continued under
the guise of "hotels" or "cabarets". Moreover, according
to newspaper reports, another gambling den has come into
existence on Yu Yuen Road and there is a likelihood of
gambling being extended into the Foreign Settlements.
If we were to make an estimate of the number
of persons who had, during the past three years, taken their
own lives or who had resorted to crime because of their
losses at these gambling dens, the Japanese should feel
much ashamed. Actually, they are not, because the huge
"protection fees" are much to their liking. Do you not,
you self-styled "master of the Orient", agree with what
we have said?

《诚言报》（评论）：—

“你同意吗？”

约一个月前，日本人“决定关闭”不良地带的赌窟。这些赌窟并未停止运营，而是改头换面，以“旅馆”或“歌舞厅”的名义继续经营。此外，据报纸报道，愚园路上又出现了一家新的赌窟，且赌博活动有可能蔓延至公共租界。
如果我们估算一下在过去三年中因在这些赌窟输钱而自杀或走上犯罪道路的人数，日本人应当感到十分羞愧。然而，他们实际上并不感到羞愧，因为巨额的“保护费”正合他们的心意。你们这些自称为“东方主人”的人，难道不同意我们的说法吗？

JAPANESE TO DEMOLISH HOUSES IN WANG KA LOONG IN WESTERN DISTRICT

The barbed wire barricades outside the wooden grilles in Chu An Pang (诸安浜), Edinburgh Road, were entirely removed yesterday. Passage was allowed between 7 a.m. and 5 p.m. The majority of residents in the lane have moved out. Two Japanese soldiers and five mercenary policemen are on guard there. According to information secured from residents in the lane, these precautionary measures may be maintained for a long time as the Japanese still do not think that Chu An Pang is a safe district.

Wang Ka Loong (汪家弄), where Sergeant Sasaki of the Japanese Army was shot, is still being guarded by two armed Japanese soldiers and four mercenary policemen. Passage is allowed between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. Though the residents in Wang Ka Loong were allowed to take out their belongings, they were not allowed to bring anything into the lane. Yesterday, an order was issued by the Japanese for the demolition of the houses in Wang Ka Loong. All residents in the lane were ordered to move out; only 20% to 30% of the residents were still living in the lane yesterday.

No British-owned buses were seen in the semi-blockaded area yesterday. A notice reading: "Terminus at Bubbling Well" has been affixed to the front part of all Route No. 1 and No. 2 buses. As Great Western Road and Edinburgh Road are still under blockade, the double-deck Route No. 14 buses are stopping at Great Western Road and Tifeng Road corner. A uniform fare of 10d for any distance is being charged.

December 17, 1940.    Morning Translation

Cheng Yien Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao, National Herald,
Chinese-American Daily News :-

DEMOLITION OF CHINESE HOUSES IN THE WESTERN DISTRICT
FOR PURPOSE OF ROAD CONSTRUCTION

Yesterday morning, the Japanese were busy constructing a new road, 40 feet wide, in the Western District to link that part of Great Western Road, where the Japanese gendarme Sasage was shot two weeks ago, with Yu Yuen Road. A high wooden door, painted white, has been erected at the entrance to New Great Western Road, where, it is believed, Japanese soldiers and mercenary policemen will be permanently stationed on guard.

The new road will be named "Sasage Road". This road will connect with another new road which starts from the spot on Jessfield Road where Corporal S. Sato was assassinated two months ago. The latter road will be named "Sato Road". It will start from the Japanese Gendarmes Headquarters at 94 Jessfield Road and terminate on Yu Yuen Road between Tifeng Road and Edinburgh Road and encircle Kinnear Road. Many Chinese houses on Jessfield Road have been pulled down for the construction of "Sato Road". Most of the residents removed after the shooting of the Japanese gendarme, but about 4,000 Chinese suffered a blockade for a period of five days. It is believed that the Japanese will build a road to connect Great Western Road with Yu Yuen Road.

Yesterday the barbed wire barricades in front of the Peh Loh Emporium (百樂商場) on Yu Yuen Road were still in position, while the number of armed Japanese soldiers have increased from two to three with about seven unarmed mercenary policemen. A passage has been opened by the Japanese at the intersection of Bubbling Well and Woo Ping Roads for vehicles and pedestrians. Several mercenary policemen and two armed Japanese soldiers are on guard. Route No. 2 buses were permitted to enter. The blockade of the area from the intersections of Bubbling Well and Great Western Roads and the south side of Great Western and Edinburgh Roads is still in force and pedestrians have to go round Bubbling Well Road and Yu Yuen Road if they want to enter the district.

Yesterday, conditions in Chu An Fang (諸安坊) off Edinburgh Road were very tense. A barbed wire barricade was erected and strict searches were being conducted by the two Japanese soldiers and five mercenary policemen of all persons entering or leaving.

Yesterday, the British-owned Route No. 2 buses could enter the district from Bubbling Well Road. Passengers of Route No. 1 double-deck buses who desired to enter the area had to alight on Bubbling Well and take the Route No. 14 buses on Yu Yuen Road.

According to unconfirmed information, the running of all the buses may be restored to-day.

西区为修筑道路拆除华人民宅

昨日上午，日军在西区忙于修筑一条宽40英尺的新路，以连接大西路（Great Western Road）上两周前日本宪兵佐佐木（Sasage）遭枪击之处与愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）。在新大西路入口处已竖起一扇漆成白色的高大木门，据信日军士兵及雇佣警员将在此永久驻守警戒。

这条新路将被命名为“佐佐木路”（Sasage Road）。该路将与另一条新路相连，后者起于两个月前曹长佐藤（S. Sato）遇刺的极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）地点。后一条路将被命名为“佐藤路”（Sato Road）。它将从位于极司菲尔路94号的日本宪兵队总部出发，终止于地丰路（Tifeng Road）与爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）之间的愚园路上，并环绕金尼尔路（Kinnear Road）。为修筑“佐藤路”，极司菲尔路上的许多华人民宅已被拆除。大多数居民在日本宪兵被枪击后迁走，但约有4,000名华人遭受了为期五天的封锁。据信，日军将修建一条道路连接大西路与愚园路。

昨日，愚园路上百乐商场（Peh Loh Emporium）前的铁丝网路障依然在原位，武装日军士兵人数已从两名增至三名，另有约七名非武装雇佣警员。日军在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）与吴平路（Woo Ping Road）交叉口为车辆和行人开辟了一条通道。数名雇佣警员和两名武装日军士兵在此警戒。允许2路公共汽车进入。大西路与静安寺路交叉口以及大西路和爱丁堡路南侧区域的封锁仍然有效，行人若想进入该区，必须绕道静安寺路和愚园路。

昨日，爱丁堡路诸安坊（Chu An Fang）内的局势非常紧张。现场竖起了铁丝网路障，两名日军士兵和五名雇佣警员对所有进出人员实施严格搜查。

昨日，英商所有的2路公共汽车可从静安寺路进入该区。欲进入该区的1路双层公共汽车乘客必须在静安寺路下车，换乘愚园路上的14路公共汽车。

据未经证实的消息，所有公共汽车的运营可能于今日恢复。

page_data.en:
December 17, 1940. Morning Translation.

Cheng Yien Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, Sin Wan Pao,
Shun Pao, National Herald :-

ASSASSINATION OF JUDGE D'HOOGHE, FRENCH MUNICIPAL ADVOCATE

At 7.15 p.m. yesterday, Judge D'Hooghe,
French Municipal Advocate, was fatally shot on Route de
Boissezon in the French Concession.
Judge D'Hooghe and his family lived in Room 34
in a foreign apartment house at No. 24 Route de Boissezon.
At 8 a.m. every day he went to his office in the French
Municipal Council and returned to his apartment at about
6 p.m. in his private motor car (Licence No.641).
After returning to his apartment from his
office yesterday afternoon, Judge D'Hooghe left his room
and went downstairs at 7.15 p.m. intending to go to a
dinner party. As he approached his private motor car
which was parked in front of the apartment, two men
suddenly appeared from the roadside and fired five or six
shots; two bullets struck him in the head and one took
effect in the waist. Judge D'Hooghe collapsed. Seeing
that they had attained their aim, the gunmen made good
their escape.
Upon receipt of a report, the French Police
sent out a large party of detectives and policemen in
Police vans and a search was made for the gunmen, but
without success. Judge D'Hooghe was immediately removed
to St. Marie Hospital. At 8 p.m. an operation was
performed, but due to his advanced age, the Judge succumbed
to his serious wounds at 8.35 p.m.
Judge D'Hooghe was 65 years of age at the time
of his death. He came to China a number of years ago,
and was once Presiding Judge in the now defunct Mixed
Court in the French Concession. He had held his present
position for 14 years.
The French Police are investigating the
cause of the assassination.

Cheng Yien Pao (comment):-

"PUTTING ON AIRS"

The people of Shanghai are clever at "putting
on airs". It is said that money can be made in this way.
Now, a certain kind of people have placed
some barbed wire "stands" in the "western suburbs".
According to foreign newspapers, a sum of $1,000,000 was
obtained by calculating the value of one stand.
The prices of commodities in Shanghai are
rising daily and the market prices in the morning and in
the evening are never the same. It is possible that
in the near future, "putting on airs" will have a bigger
value.
page_data.zh:
1940年12月17日。晨间译稿。

《诚言报》、《中美日报》、《新闻报》、
《申报》、《国民公报》：

法国公董局律师德胡格法官遇刺身亡

昨日下午7时15分，法国公董局律师德胡格（D'Hooghe）法官在法租界布西雄路（Route de Boissezon）遭枪击，伤重不治。

德胡格法官及其家属居住在布西雄路24号一幢外侨公寓的34室。他每日上午8时前往法国公董局办公室办公，并于下午6时许乘坐私人汽车（牌照号641）返回寓所。

昨日下午从办公室返回寓所后，德胡格法官于晚上7时15分离开房间下楼，拟赴晚宴。当他走近停在公寓门前的私人汽车时，两名男子突然从路边出现，连开五至六枪；两颗子弹击中其头部，一颗击中腰部。德胡格法官随即倒地。枪手见目的已达，便迅速逃逸。

接报后，法国警方派出大批侦探及警员，乘警车出动搜捕枪手，但未有收获。德胡格法官被立即送往圣玛丽医院（St. Marie Hospital）。晚8时进行手术，但因年事已高，法官于晚8时35分因伤势过重去世。

德胡格法官去世时年65岁。他于数年前来到中国，曾担任现已撤销的法租界会审公廨主审法官。他担任现职已有14年。

法国警方正在调查此次刺杀案的起因。

《诚言报》评论：

“摆架子”

上海人善于“摆架子”。据说以此可以牟利。

如今，某些人在“西郊”设置了一些带刺铁丝网“岗哨”。据外文报纸称，按每个岗哨的价值计算，共获款100万元。

上海物价日日上涨，早晚市价各不相同。或许在不久的将来，“摆架子”会有更大的价值。

page_data.en:
December 15, 194.
Morning Translation.

Shen Tien Pao -

MOST OF THE BLOCK DEL NEA IN THE WESTERN DISTRICT OPENED
YESTERDAY

After its blockade by the Japanese for nearly
two weeks, the Western District has been opened since
yesterday morning. However, according to information secured
by this paper, the Japanese gendarmes continued to prevent
the operation of the British-owned buses on Yu Yuen Road
yesterday and forced the conductors to alight from the
vehicles and kneel before them for a while before they were
allowed to proceed on their way.
At about 9 p.m. yesterday an inspection was
made by our reporter in the Western District in the course
of which he noticed that the south side of the intersection
of Great Western Road and Edinburgh Road was still closed,
while barbed wire entanglements at certain small passages
were still present. According to information from reliable
sources, the Japanese-owned buses are still conducting
operations in the Western District with the connivance of
the Japanese soldiers. This is clear evidence of deliberate
trespass upon the monopolistic rights enjoyed by the China
General Omnibus Company. Negotiations are at present
proceeding between the Shanghai Municipal Council and the
Japanese authorities, but up to the present no result has
been attained.

Cheng Yien Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, National Herald,
Sin Wan Pao and Shun Pao :-

According to information secured by the Dah
Chung News Agency, following the Japanese blockade of the
area bordering Avenue Haig, Great Western Road, Edinburgh
Road and Yu Yuen Road as a result of the attack on a Japanese
gendarme named Sasaki on Great Western Road on November 30,
repeated negotiations have been conducted by the local
Consular Body with the Japanese authorities, with the result
that the area was once more thrown open to the public at
11.40 a.m. yesterday. Routes No. 1 and 2 buses have now
resumed operations within the area.
However, there are still two places where
the barbed wire barricades are present, namely, one at the
south side of the corner of Great Western Road and Edinburgh
Road and another between the Country Hospital and the Frazer
Automobile Company. They are, however, expected to be
removed within a day or two. The wooden grille erected at
Chung Shing Tsung (中興總) at Hsing Ka Long (興家弄),
Great Western Road, is still closed with two mercenary
policemen on guard, while the alleyways along Chu An Pang
(朱安浜), Edinburgh Road, which the Japanese regard as the
cesspool of terroristic elements, are likewise blockaded
as usual. At 4 p.m. yesterday, a search was conducted at
the place by Japanese gendarmes in company with mercenary
policemen. Shops at the place have all resumed business,
while the gambling dens, "constitution rooms" and hwp hwei
lottery agencies have likewise once more resumed their illegal
operations and are extending their devilish hands to make
good what they have lost during the period of the blockade.
page_data.zh:
194.年12月15日。
晨间译稿。

《申报》——

西区大部分封锁区域昨日开放

在被日军封锁近两周后，西区自昨日上午起已重新开放。然而，据本报获得的消息，日本宪兵昨日继续阻止英资公共汽车在愚园路运营，并强迫售票员下车，在他们面前跪了一段时间后，才允许车辆继续前行。
昨晚约9时，本报记者对西区进行了视察，期间注意到大西路与爱丁堡路交叉口的南侧仍然封闭，某些小通道处的铁丝网障碍物依然存在。据可靠消息来源称，日资公共汽车在日本士兵的纵容下，仍在西区运营。这显然是故意侵犯中国公共汽车公司所享有的垄断权的行为。目前，上海公共租界工部局与日本当局正在进行谈判，但截至目前尚未取得任何结果。

《诚言报》、《中美日报》、《国民新闻》、《新闻报》及《顺报》：

据大公通讯社获得的消息，继11月30日一名名为佐佐木（Sasaki）的日本宪兵在大西路遇袭后，日军封锁了毗邻海格路、大西路、爱丁堡路及愚园路的区域，当地领事团随后与日本当局进行了多次谈判，结果是该区域于昨日上午11时40分再次向公众开放。1路和2路公共汽车现已在该区域内恢复运营。
然而，仍有两处存在铁丝网路障，一处在 大西路与爱丁堡路拐角处的南侧，另一处在乡村医院（Country Hospital）与弗雷泽汽车公司（Frazer Automobile Company）之间。不过，预计这些路障将在一两天内拆除。位于大西路兴家弄中兴总（Chung Shing Tsung）设立的木制格栅门仍然关闭，由两名雇佣警察守卫；而沿爱丁堡路朱安浜（Chu An Pang）的小巷，被日本人视为恐怖分子的藏污纳垢之地，也同样像往常一样被封锁。昨日下午4时，日本宪兵会同雇佣警察对该地进行了搜查。该地的商铺均已恢复营业，而赌场、“麻将室”以及花会彩票代理处也再次恢复了非法活动，正伸出魔爪以弥补在封锁期间的损失。

page_data.en:
December 15, 194.
Morning Translation

Central China Daily News, New China Daily News, Kuo Min Daily
News, Ming Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, Chen Yen Pao,
National Herald, Shun Pao and Sin Wan Pao :-

F.M.P. CHINESE POLICEMEN GET BETTER TREATMENT

The question of the allowance of Chinese
policemen of the French Police was settled yesterday
afternoon. The entire body of Chinese policemen were
satisfied with the present increase in allowance.
In fact, an increase of the allowance of
the Chinese policemen had already been under the consideration
of the French authorities prior to the strike of the Chinese
policemen. After the Chinese policemen resumed duty, the
Commissioner of the French Police requested the French
Municipal Council to give an early announcement of the
measures taken to increase the allowance of the Chinese
policemen so that they can work with an easy mind. An
announcement of the measures, which were reached after careful
discussions by the F.M.C., was originally to have been made
on December 13, but owing to the lack of time the announcement
was made yesterday. The report of an interview with the
Police authorities at 9 a.m. yesterday by the representatives
of the Chinese policemen requesting an early settlement of
the matter was untrue.
It is learned that in accordance with the
new measures announced at 4 p.m. yesterday, the allowance
granted to the Chinese policemen has been increased from
70% to 140% and the special reward has been increased from
$6 to $25. After the enforcement of the new measures, a
Chinese policeman of the lowest rank, namely, a 5th Class
Probationary Constable, will receive a pay of more than
$120, including a rice allowance of half "zar" of rice, per
mensem. It is also learned that with effect from January
next year, every probationary Chinese policeman will be
granted an increase of $2 in wages. With regard to the
other demands submitted by the Chinese policemen, the
authorities have intimated that they will be enforced
gradually.

Central China Daily News, New China Daily News, Chinese-American
Daily News, Cheng Hsien Pao, National Herald, Sin Wan Pao, Shun
Pao of December 14:-

CUSTOMS REVENUE GUARDS WILL GET BETTER TREATMENT

The monthly wages of the entire body of
revenue guards of the Maritime Customs are very low and they
get an increase of only $1 per year. Owing to the
difficulties of maintaining their living at the present high
prices of commodities, the entire body of revenue guards
recently sent representatives to interview Commissioner
Lawford and requested that their wages be increased to the
same level as the employees and workers of the Post Office
in Shanghai. The Customs authorities are now of the opinion
that the demands of the revenue guards are reasonable. It
is learned that within every sphere the wages of all low
class employees of the Customs will be raised. It is said
that an improvement will be put into force next year.
P.T.O.
page_data.zh:
194.年12月15日。
晨间译稿

《华中日报》、《新中国日报》、《国民日报》、《明报》、《中美日报》、《晨报》、《国民新闻报》、《申报》及《新闻报》：

法租界巡捕房华籍巡捕待遇改善

法租界巡捕房华籍巡捕的津贴问题已于昨日下午解决。全体华籍巡捕对目前的津贴增加表示满意。
事实上，在华籍巡捕罢工之前，法国当局已在考虑增加华籍巡捕的津贴。华籍巡捕复职后，法租界巡捕房总监请求法公董局尽早公布增加华籍巡捕津贴的措施，以便他们能安心工作。经法公董局仔细讨论后达成的措施公告，原定于12月13日发布，但因时间不足，公告于昨日发布。有关华籍巡捕代表于昨日上午9时面见警务当局要求尽早解决此事的报道不实。
据悉，根据昨日下午4时公布的新措施，发给华籍巡捕的津贴已从70%增至140%，特别奖金从6元增至25元。实施新措施后，最低级别的华籍巡捕，即五等试用巡捕，每月收入将超过120元，其中包括半“扎”（zar）大米的米贴。另悉，自明年一月起，每名华籍试用巡捕的工资将增加2元。关于华籍巡捕提出的其他要求，当局暗示将逐步实施。

12月14日的《华中日报》、《新中国日报》、《中美日报》、《诚言报》、《国民新闻报》、《新闻报》、《申报》：

海关缉私卫队待遇改善

海关全体缉私卫队的月薪很低，每年仅增加1元。由于在当前高昂的物价下维持生活困难，全体缉私卫队最近派出代表面见拉福德（Lawford）总监，要求将其工资提高至与上海邮局雇员和工人相同的水平。海关当局目前认为缉私卫队的要求是合理的。据悉，海关所有低级雇员的工资将在各个部门予以提高。据说改进措施将于明年生效。

page_data.en:
December 15, 1940. Morning Translation.

In connection with the interference with the Chinese watchmen and the compulsory enforcement of an order compelling ricsha coolies to take out licences in the Western District by the Japanese gendarmes, negotiations were opened with the Japanese authorities by the S.M.C. yesterday. According to an official statement issued by the Publicity Office of the S.M.C., a letter has been sent to the Japanese Consul-General calling his attention to both matters.

The blockade has resulted in considerable impairment of the monopolistic rights of traffic in the Western District enjoyed by the International Settlement. The operation of Japanese-owned buses on Yu Yuen Road and Great Western Road has given rise to much inconvenience and annoyance to the Settlement authorities and the residents. Since yesterday morning, the blockade has been lifted. According to reliable quarters, the blockade was lifted due to either of the following grounds:-
(1) Since the blockade, the China Club on Great Western Road and the Hwa Loh Club (花樂會) on Yu Yuen Road, both being large gambling dens, have suffered considerable losses. Consequently, they have offered a huge sum as a passage money. Though the exact amount is unknown, it is said to be somewhere round $500,000.
(2). Though the Japanese have not yet disclosed the result of their purge in the cesspool of terroristic elements at Waung Ka Loong and Edinburgh Road, they have now considered it unnecessary to blockade so large an area. Consequently, the outer regions have been reopened but Waung Ka Loong, etc. were still closed yesterday.

At about 11 a.m. yesterday, a couple of buses each of the Routes No. 1 and 9 of the China General Omnibus Company resumed operations on Yu Yuen Road; in the afternoon Route No. 9 buses and Route No. 20 railless cars likewise resumed operations along Great Western Road and Yu Yuen Road. None of the so-called Western District People's buses were noticed travelling in the Western District yesterday. It is said that the loss suffered by the China General Omnibus Co. and the Shanghai Tramway Co. amounted altogether to approximately $80,000. Meanwhile, ricshas bearing Settlement licences are still denied entrance into the outlying roads area, unless they are issued with "City Government licences" or have affixed on the back the characters "with special permission from the Western District Traffic Committee."

In connection with the illegal operation of Japanese-owned buses in the blockaded area in the Western District, a protest was lodged with the Japanese Consul-General by the S.M.C. at beginning of this week, but no reply has yet been received by the Council to its protest. However, it is generally expected that the Japanese-owned buses will cease operations in the area because it has already been declared by the Japanese authorities that this operation was but a temporary arrangement.

Cheng Yien Pao (comment) :-

The Reopening of the Western District

After two weeks of blockade, the "western corner" was finally reopened yesterday morning. In view of the duration and the gravity of the blockade, the reopening has conveyed a "special feeling" to the public.

P. T. O.
page_data.zh:
1940年12月15日。晨间译稿。

针对日本宪兵干涉中国巡捕，并在西区强制推行责令人力车夫领取执照的命令一事，工部局于昨日与日本当局展开交涉。据工部局新闻处发布的官方声明称，已致函日本总领事，提请其注意上述两事。

封锁导致国际租界在西区享有的交通垄断权受到严重损害。日资巴士在愚园路和大西路（Great Western Road）的运营，给租界当局及居民带来诸多不便与困扰。自昨晨起，封锁已解除。据可靠消息来源，封锁解除系出于以下任一原因：
(1) 自封锁以来，位于大西路的“中国总会”（China Club）和位于愚园路的“花乐会”（Hwa Loh Club），这两处大型赌博场所均遭受重大损失。因此，它们提供了一笔巨款作为通行费。虽确切金额不详，但据悉约为50万元。
(2) 尽管日本人尚未公布其在汪家弄（Waung Ka Loong）和爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）恐怖分子巢穴进行清洗的结果，但他们现在认为没有必要对如此大的区域实施封锁。因此，外围地区已重新开放，但汪家弄等地昨日仍处于关闭状态。

昨日上午11时许，英商中国公共汽车公司（China General Omnibus Company）第1路和第9路的两辆巴士在愚园路恢复运营；下午，第9路巴士和第20路无轨电车亦沿大西路和愚园路恢复运营。昨日在西区未发现有所谓的“西区人民巴士”行驶。据悉，英商中国公共汽车公司与上海电车公司（Shanghai Tramway Co.）的损失总额约为8万元。与此同时，悬挂租界执照的人力车仍被禁止进入外围道路区域，除非其持有“市政府执照”，或在车尾贴有“经西区交通委员会特许”字样。

针对日资巴士在西区封锁区域内非法运营一事，工部局已于本周初向日本总领事提出抗议，但工部局尚未收到对其抗议的答复。然而，普遍预计日资巴士将停止在该区域的运营，因为日本当局已宣布此运营仅为临时安排。

《诚言报》评论：

西区重开

经过两周的封锁，“西角”终于于昨晨重新开放。鉴于封锁持续时间之长及事态之严重，此次重开给公众传达了一种“特殊的感觉”。

page_data.en:
December 15, 1940. Morning Translation.

The cause of the reopening is unknown. However,
a study of the reports appearing in local newspapers
previously and of the statistics of the "remarkable
performances" conducted during the period of the blockade,
will offer no difficulty in understanding the cause of the
blockade.

According to Press reports, pedestrians
desiring passage were required to pay a "passage money"
ranging from $0.20 to $0.50. In all the blockade lasted
14 days. If it is taken into account that every day only
1,000 pedestrians were given passage in this manner, the
sum acquired would have been quite considerable.

"Japanese-owned buses are operating along Yu
Yuen Road and are doing quite good business." "The routes
of the British-owned buses have all been shortened and
have stopped travelling in the blockaded area." These are
two other headings appearing in newspapers. It is needless
to point out the facts as the readers must have already
understood them well.

According to them, the blockade was enforced
because they desired to effect the arrest of the culprits.
However, by common sense, in view of the fact that a number
of places in the blockaded area had been reopened and closed
several times during the blockade, it seems unlikely that
they could have been so foolish as to endeavour to effect
the apprehension of the culprits after the reopening of
the place.

According to a report appearing in this paper,
the China Club has already offered a sum of $500,000 to a
certain party as "protection fee" and the blockade would
soon be lifted.

Now the blockaded area has been reopened. All
the facts surrounding this blockade have shown the true
description of the master of the "new order."
page_data.zh:
1940年12月15日。晨间译文。

重新开放的原因尚不清楚。然而，通过研究此前当地报纸上刊登的报道，以及封锁期间进行的“显著行动”的统计数据，就不难理解实施封锁的原因。

据新闻报道，希望通行的行人被要求支付0.20至0.50元不等的“过路费”。封锁总共持续了14天。如果考虑到每天仅有1,000名行人以这种方式获准通行，所获得的金额将相当可观。

“日资巴士在愚园路运营，生意相当兴隆。”“英资巴士的路线均已缩短，并停止在封锁区域内行驶。”这是报纸上出现的另外两个标题。事实无需赘述，读者想必已十分清楚。

据称，实施封锁是因为他们希望逮捕罪犯。然而，根据常识，鉴于封锁区域内的多处地点在封锁期间曾多次开放又关闭，他们似乎不太可能愚蠢到试图在某个地点重新开放后才去抓捕罪犯。

据本报一篇报道，中国总会（China Club）已向某方提供50万元作为“保护费”，封锁即将解除。

目前，封锁区域已经重新开放。围绕此次封锁的所有事实，都已对这位“新秩序”的主宰者作出了真实的写照。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
Sp. Br. REGISTRY

blockade Dec

December 12, 1940.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH）

TIRIKU SHIMPO :-

REFUTATION OF EXAGGERATED REPORTS

Foreign newspapers and anti-Japanese
Chinese newspapers in the Settlements are publishing
exaggerated reports to incite the people against the joint
action taken in the Western District by Japan and China
towards lawless elements. It is alleged that as a
result of the blockade of the district, the residents
there are suffering from acute shortage of foodstuffs
while the China Bus Company and the Tramway Company are
sustaining an enormous loss. But actually, conditions
in the District are totally different from what these
newspapers say.
As for the Western District People's
Omnibus Company, it is established by leading persons in
the blockaded area and is operating its buses on Yu Yuen
Road and Great Western Road thereby considerably
alleviating traffic congestion.
Although the China Bus Company and
the Tramway Company are strongly criticizing the alleged
encroachment upon their rights, they have taken advantage
of the disorder and confusion created by the former
Shanghai Incident and acquired the right to run their
buses and trams in this District in defiance of the strong
objection raised by the Chinese side. On these grounds,
they have no basis on which to lay their claim for their
legal rights.

特别科登记室

封锁 十二月

1940年12月12日。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别科）

《日日新闻》：

驳斥夸大报道

租界内的外文报纸及反华（原文为anti-Japanese，依语境及当时日方立场应指反日）中文报纸正在发布夸大报道，煽动民众反对日本与中国在西区针对不法分子采取的联合行动。这些报纸声称，由于对该地区实施封锁，当地居民正遭受食品严重短缺之苦，同时中华巴士公司与电车公司也正蒙受巨大损失。然而实际上，该地区的情况与这些报纸所说的截然不同。

至于西区人民公共汽车公司，它是由被封锁区域内的知名人士创办的，目前在愚园路和大西路运营公共汽车，从而大大缓解了交通拥堵状况。

尽管中华巴士公司和电车公司强烈批评所谓对其权利的侵犯，但它们却利用了此前“上海事变”造成的混乱局面，不顾中方提出的强烈反对，攫取了在该地区运营公共汽车和电车的权利。基于这些理由，它们主张其合法权利是毫无根据的。

page_data.en:
December 12, 1940. Afternoon Translation

National Herald (comment) :-

ABANDONMENT OF THE APPEASEMENT POLICY

Since the outlying road areas have been blockaded, the transportation franchise granted by the S.M.C. has been violated and policemen have been assaulted and insulted. A certain party is again trying to collect ricsha licence fees. Last night, a Route No. 7 bus was attacked on Edinburgh Road.
A foreign observer has declared that this was a planned and organized attempt of the Japanese to partition the administrative rights of the S.M.C. in the Western District, with the object of tearing up the Yangkingpang Land Regulations.
As regards the infringement of the transportation franchise, the S.M.C. opened negotiations the day before yesterday. With reference to the assaulting and insulting of policemen, it is said that a protest will be delivered to-day. It is not known what the reply of the Japanese will be.
As the S.M.C. is an executive organization formed according to the Yangkingpang Land Regulations, it seems that the S.M.C. should not permit the Japanese to break the Regulations. The S.M.C. should abandon its long-adopted appeasement policy and open strong negotiations with the Japanese. Should it fail, the S.M.C. must ask the Consular Body and the foreign governments concerned for assistance, so as to bring the matter to the attention of the Japanese Government.
page_data.zh:
1940年12月12日。下午译文

《国民新闻报》（评论）：

放弃绥靖政策

自外围道路区域被封锁以来，上海公共租界工部局授予的交通专营权遭到侵犯，警察亦遭殴打和侮辱。某方再次试图收取人力车执照费。昨晚，一辆7路公共汽车在爱丁堡路遭到袭击。
一位外国观察家宣称，这是日本人有计划、有组织地企图分割上海公共租界工部局在西区行政权的行动，其目的在于撕毁《洋泾浜土地章程》。
关于交通专营权受侵犯一事，上海公共租界工部局已于前日开启谈判。至于警察遭殴打和侮辱一事，据悉将于今日提出抗议。日方的答复尚不得而知。
鉴于上海公共租界工部局是依据《洋泾浜土地章程》成立的执行机构，工部局似乎不应允许日本人破坏该章程。工部局应放弃长期采取的绥靖政策，与日方展开强硬谈判。若谈判失败，工部局必须向领事团及相关外国政府寻求援助，以便将此事项提请日本政府注意。

page_data.en:
December 1., 1940.
Morning Translation.
Sheng Yien Pao :-
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S- B. REGISTRY
CONDITIONS IN THE WESTERN DISTRICT
It was learned by a reporter of this paper
that the situation in the blockaded area in the Western
District became worse yesterday. Traffic from Edinburgh
Road to Avenue Haig was again interrupted, while Great
Western Road and other places are still under blockade.
Pedestrians are complaining for they have to make a long
detour. Business in the Farrens Club was bad yesterday. It
is said that patriotic slogans were discovered yesterday
written on the walls of the Li Chao Fang (李兆坊) alleyway
off Yu Yuen Road. A search was conducted by the Japanese
soldiers, but it had no result. The Japanese gendarmes and
mercenary policemen are continuing to search Chinese residences.
Yesterday some ten primary school students
inside Lane 909, Yu Yuen Road, were noticed throwing
newspapers at one another. The Japanese gendarmes examined
the newspapers and found that all these newspapers were
supporters of justice. Becoming angry, the Japanese tried to
arrest the students, but the latter escaped. The gendarmes
knocked at the doors of the houses in the alleyway with the
object of carrying out a search but when they found that they
could not do anything, they blockaded the alleyway. As their
food supplies are running out, the residents are in danger
of starvation.
Another report states that the British-owned
buses which have been running in the Western District were
suddenly attacked by a large number of bad elements. A Route
No. 7 bus which had stopped at a terminus near the corner of
Edinburgh Road and Avenue Haig was attacked by a number of
bad elements who threw bricks and tiles into the bus. The
driver and conductor of the bus remonstrated, but no heed
was paid to them. The driver, Yi Zung-yien (易人化), aged
37, native of Anhwei, residing at No. 5, Zung Teh Li
(仁德里), Brenan Road, was injured on the head and was sent
to the Red Cross Hospital. It is believed that the bad elements
had been instigated into carrying out such activities with the
object of harming the interests of foreigners.
According to information secured from
foreign sources, the S.M.C. did not lodge a protest yesterday
with the Japanese authorities against the assault of a Chinese
Police Officer of the S.M.P. by Japanese gendarmes. According
to a spokesman of the Council, a protest may be handed to the
Japanese this morning.
As regards the operation of Japanese-owned
buses in the Western District, the Chairman of the S.M.C.
opened negotiations with the Japanese Consul-General on
December 10.
It was learned by a reporter of the Dah
Chung News Agency that this matter was discussed at the Council
meeting yesterday afternoon. It is said that after it had
made an investigation, the Japanese Consulate replied that
Japanese official circles were unaware of the matter as the
running of the Japanese-owned buses in the Western District
was an individual act.
It is said that negotiations will be opened,
while the Japanese Councillors will be asked to make an
investigation into this affair.
P.T.O.

1940年12月1日。
晨间译稿。
《申彦报》：
上海公共租界工部局警务处
S-B 登记处
西区局势
本报记者从可靠渠道获悉，昨日西区封锁区内的局势进一步恶化。从爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）至海格路（Avenue Haig）的交通再次中断，而大西路（Great Western Road）及其他地区仍处于封锁状态。行人怨声载道，因为他们不得不绕远路。法伦斯俱乐部（Farrens Club）昨日的生意惨淡。据悉，昨日在愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）旁的李兆坊弄堂墙壁上发现了爱国标语。日本士兵进行了搜查，但一无所获。日本宪兵和雇佣警探继续搜查中国居民的住宅。
昨日，有人注意到愚园路909弄内约有十名小学生在互相投掷报纸。日本宪兵检查了这些报纸，发现所有报纸均持正义立场。日本人勃然大怒，试图逮捕这些学生，但学生们逃脱了。宪兵敲击弄堂内各户房门，意图进行搜查，但在发现无法采取任何行动后，他们封锁了该弄堂。由于食物供应即将耗尽，居民面临饥饿的危险。
另有报告称，此前在西区运营的英资公交车突然遭到大量不良分子的袭击。一辆7路公交车停在爱丁堡路与海格路转角附近的终点站时，遭到一群不良分子的袭击，这些人向车内投掷砖瓦。公交车司机和售票员提出抗议，但未予理睬。司机易人化（Yi Zung-yien），37岁，安徽籍，居住在贝伦路（Brenan Road）仁德里5号，头部受伤，被送往红十字会医院。据信，这些不良分子是受人指使进行此类活动，旨在损害外国人的利益。
据从外方获得的消息，工部局昨日未就日本宪兵袭击工部局警务处一名华籍巡捕一事向日本当局提出抗议。据工部局发言人称，抗议书可能于今日上午递交给日方。
关于日资公交车在西区的运营问题，工部局主席已于12月10日与日本总领事展开谈判。
大中通讯社记者从可靠渠道获悉，此事在昨日下午的工部局会议上进行了讨论。据悉，经调查后，日本领事馆回复称，日本官方对此事并不知情，因为日资公交车在西区的运营属于个人行为。
据悉，谈判即将展开，同时将要求日本籍董事对此事进行调查。

December 11, 1940. Morning Translation.

Cheng Yien Pao (brief comment) :-

It is reported that a number of patriotic
slogans were found at Li Chao Fang, Yu Yuan Road, yesterday.
The Japanese soldiers were highly indignant and conducted
a vigorous search in the neighbourhood but without result.

Cheng Yien Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, National Herald,
Sin Han Pao and Shun Pao :-

"CHINESE POLICEMEN IN FRENCH CONCESSION ON STRIKE YESTERDAY
MORNING ; 17 DEMANDS FOR BETTER TREATMENT SUBMITTED ;
AUTHORITIES PROMISE TO GIVE REPLY WITHOUT 3 OR 4 DAYS"

The entire body of Chinese policemen in the
French Concession, who are finding it difficult to maintain
their livelihood with their small pay, recently submitted,
verbally, to the French authorities a demand for an increase
of wages. As no formal reply has been given by the French
authorities, 150 Chinese policemen of Lokawei Police Station
went on strike at 8.45 a.m. yesterday and their action was
followed by the 140 Chinese policemen in other Stations.
As a result of the strike, traffic in the
French Concession was in great disorder as no policemen were
on traffic duty, but the situation improved after employees
of the French Tramway Company and French policemen took over
the traffic duty.
The Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner of
the French Police immediately held a conference with the
Chinese policemen of Lokawei Station. 120 Chinese policemen
were present.
The Commissioner of the French Police stated
the French authorities were paying attention to the liveli-
hood of the Chinese policemen owing to the sharp increases
in the prices of commodities and that measures for their
better treatment were already under consideration. The
Commissioner then asked the Chinese policemen on strike to
submit their demands.
Chinese policemen Nos. 158, 164 and 598 were
then elected representatives of the policemen and they
handed the demands to the Commissioner.
The Commissioner stated that he would give
guarantee a satisfactory reply to the strikers within three
or four days and expressed the hope that the Chinese policemen,
would, for the sake of peace and good order, immediately
resume duty.
The strikers were satisfied with the
Commissioner's promise and resumed duty at once.
Yesterday morning, a Chinese policeman
propagating a strike at the corner of Route Stanislas
Chevalier and Rue Massenet was arrested by white Russian
detectives but he was released before the Chinese policemen
on strike resumed duty.
The following are the demands submitted by
the entire body of Chinese policemen:-
(1) The formation of a French Concession
Chinese Policemen's Mutual Aid Association.
page_data.zh:
1940年12月11日。晨间译报。

《诚言报》（简评）：

据报，昨日在李朝坊（音译）、愚园路发现多条爱国标语。日军士兵极为愤慨，在附近进行了严密搜查，但一无所获。

《诚言报》、《中美日报》、《国民新闻报》、《新汉报》及《申报》：

“法租界华捕昨晨罢工；提交改善待遇之十七条要求；当局承诺三至四日内答复”

法租界全体华警因薪俸微薄，难以维持生计，近期口头向法方当局提出加薪要求。由于法方当局未给予正式答复，昨天上午8时45分，卢家湾巡捕房的150名华警率先罢工，其他巡捕房的140名华警随即跟进。罢工导致法租界交通陷入极大混乱，因无警察执行交通勤务，但在法国电车公司员工及法籍警察接手交通指挥后，局势得以改善。

法租界警务处总监及副总监立即与卢家湾巡捕房的华警举行会议。120名华警出席了会议。

法租界警务处总监表示，鉴于物价急剧上涨，法方当局正关注华警的生计问题，且改善其待遇的措施已在考虑之中。随后，总监要求罢工的华警提交具体要求。

随后，第158号、164号及598号华警被选为警察代表，他们将要求书递交给总监。

总监表示，保证在三至四天内向罢工者给予令人满意的答复，并希望华警为了和平与良好秩序，立即复职。

罢工者对总监的承诺表示满意，并立即恢复执勤。

昨晨，一名在斯坦尼斯拉斯·谢瓦利埃路（Route Stanislas Chevalier）与马斯内路（Rue Massenet）拐角处鼓动罢工的华警被白俄侦探逮捕，但在罢工华警恢复执勤前，该人已被释放。

以下是全体华警提交的要求：
(1) 成立法租界华警互助会。

page_data.en:
Chinese-American Daily News, Shun Pao, Cheng Yih Pao,
National Herald :- 9/17/40

"CITY POLICEMAN KNOCKED DOWN BY MOTOR CYCLE : SETTLEMENT
DETECTIVES AND POLICEMEN MAKING INVESTIGATIONS ARE
DETAINED."

At 9 p.m. yesterday, Liu Ngoo-cho (刘玉书),
a City policeman on post duty at the intersection of
Edinburgh Road and Kinnear Road in the Western District,
was knocked down by a motor cycle. Another City
policeman telephoned Bubbling Well Police Station requesting
it to send an ambulance to remove the injured policeman
to the Second St. Luke's Hospital on Brenan Road for
treatment. Bubbling Well Police Station detailed more
than ten Chinese and foreign detectives and policemen to blockad
the scene to make an investigation. However, they were
obstructed by Japanese gendarmes who removed their pistols
and took the party of officers to the Japanese Gendarmerie
Headquarters at 94 Jessfield Road.
Upon receipt of a report, Bubbling Well
Police Station detailed officers to explain away any
misunderstanding. The Chinese and foreign officers were
released at 11 p.m. with their pistols restored.
（印：SPECIAL BRANCH I.O.）
page_data.zh:
《中美日报》、《申报》、《诚益报》、
《国民导报》：1940年9月17日

“华捕被摩托车撞倒：租界巡捕与侦探进行调查时被扣留。”

昨晚九时，西区爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）与金尼尔路（Kinnear Road）交叉口执勤的华捕刘玉书（Liu Ngoo-cho），被一辆摩托车撞倒。另一名华捕致电静安寺捕房，请求派遣救护车将受伤警员送往勃伦南路（Brenan Road）的第二圣卢克医院（Second St. Luke's Hospital）接受治疗。静安寺捕房调派十余名中西探员及巡捕封锁现场以展开调查。然而，他们遭到日本宪兵阻拦，宪兵收缴了他们的手枪，并将这队警员带往杰斯菲尔德路（Jessfield Road）94号的日本宪兵队总部。

接获报告后，静安寺捕房调派人员前去解释以消除任何误会。中西警员于当晚十一时获释，手枪亦被归还。
（印：特别分部情报官）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE

6-12-40 P.m.

Cheng Yien Pao (comment) :-
"THE MAINTENANCE OF PEACE AND GOOD ORDER"
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH）
Field unit
recent
assassination
case

We distinctly recall that when shooting cases were occurring repeatedly in the two Foreign Settlements, the Japanese strongly criticized the inefficiency of the Police Forces of the Foreign Settlements and suggested that Japanese be allowed to maintain peace and good order in the Foreign Settlements.
Of late many cases of assassination have taken place in Hongkew and in the Western District where peace and good order is being maintained by Japanese. Furthermore, the victims in these cases were Japanese army or naval officers. What is stranger still is that ten unsolved cases have occurred and in each case the assailant or assailants had been able to make good their escape.
From this one may come to the conclusion that the Japanese troops and the mercenary police who are so skillful in maintaining peace and good order have failed to solve these cases and can only shake their heads and sigh.
Of late, the Japanese seemed to have become wiser. They have resorted to the method of blockading an area. They may blockade Hongkew to-day and the Western District to-morrow; but the people living in these areas have to undergo indescribable suffering. At first mercenary policemen would resort to extortion and this would be followed by the running of buses operated by Japanese. However, they seem to have overlooked the point that after all the people have removed, there would be no peace and good order to be maintained. In that event, they would only have the work of protecting themselves.

1940年12月6日 下午

程艳宝（音译）（评论）：
“维持和平与良好秩序”
（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别处）
外勤组
近期
暗杀
案件

我们清楚地记得，当两外国租界内枪击案频发时，日本人强烈批评外国租界警队效率低下，并建议允许日本人负责维持外国租界的和平与良好秩序。
近来，在由日本人维持和平与良好秩序的虹口及西区，发生了多起暗杀案件。此外，这些案件的受害者均为日本陆海军军官。更为奇怪的是，已有十起案件未破，且在每起案件中，行凶者均成功逃脱。
由此可以得出结论，那些在维持和平与良好秩序方面如此娴熟的日军及雇佣警察，未能侦破这些案件，只能摇头叹息。
近来，日本人似乎变得聪明了一些。他们采取了封锁区域的方法。他们可能今天封锁虹口，明天封锁西区；但居住在这些区域的民众不得不遭受难以言喻的痛苦。起初，雇佣警察会进行勒索，随后则是运营由日本人经营的公共汽车。然而，他们似乎忽略了一点，即一旦民众全部迁离，也就没有所谓的和平与良好秩序需要维持了。在那种情况下，他们只剩下保护自己的工作。

ASSISTANT COMMISSIONER
SPECIAL BRANCH

December 4, 1940.

Chinese-American Daily News, Cheng Yien Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Shun
Pao, National Herald :-

CONSULAR BODY OPENS NEGOTIATIONS OVER BLOCKADE OF
WESTERN DISTRICT

Following the shooting of a Japanese gendarme
on Great Western Road in the Western District on November 30,
the Japanese authorities immediately blockaded an area
bounded by Tifeng Road, Great Western Road, Edinburgh Road
and Yu Yuen Road. Both Chinese and foreign residents
living in the blockaded areas were prohibited from leaving.
On the evening of December 2, the Japanese
extended the blockade to the front of the Paramount Ballroom
and barbed wire barricades were placed on the border of
the Settlement. The 100,000 residents living in the
blockaded areas are faced with difficulties of securing
food supplies.

It is said that the S.M.C. has opened
negotiations with the Japanese. According to Major Bourne,
Commissioner of S.M.P., the negotiations held on the
morning of December 3 for the immediate removal of the
blockade had no result, but measures were drawn up restricting
the movements of Chinese and foreign residents, but they
were less severe in character.

On December 3, Japanese soldiers and gendarmes
and Chinese policemen with fixed bayonets patrolled the
blockaded areas in the Western District. Chinese people
were prohibited from leaving or entering nor were foodstuffs
allowed to be sent in. It was said that teachers and
students would be permitted free access, but this has been
found to be untrue. Foreigners are permitted to pass the
barricades.

Large and small gambling dens and shops in
the blockaded areas are all closed. The price of rice
in the area has been increased considerably.

Out of consideration for the safety of the
Chinese and foreign residents in the blockaded area,
the S.M.C. opened negotiations with the Japanese on the
morning of December 3 with the object of procuring freedom
of access for the residents. In the meantime, the Senior
Consul has been requested to open negotiations with the
Japanese Consul-General so that an early settlement of the
trouble might be found.

The Senior Consul says that the Japanese
Consul-General is in sympathy with the residents, but in
his letter of reply, received at 2 p.m. that day,
he states that the restrictions have been adopted in
order to facilitate the arrest of the murderers and that
the blockade would not be removed until such time as
the Japanese authorities come to the conclusion that
it would be impossible to arrest the murderers.

The Japanese Police officer assisting in the
negotiations says that the reply received from the
Japanese authorities indicates that the blockade would
not be removed for some time to come and that there is
even a possibility of the blockade being continued for
two or three weeks.

《中美日报》、《诚言报》、《新闻报》、《申报》、《国民导报》：

领事团就西区封锁一事展开谈判

继 11 月 30 日一名日本宪兵在西区大西路（Great Western Road）遭枪击后，日本当局立即封锁了由蒂丰路（Tifeng Road）、大西路、爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）和愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）所围成的区域。居住在封锁区内的中外居民均被禁止离开。12 月 2 日晚，日本人将封锁线延伸至百乐门舞厅（Paramount Ballroom）前方，并在租界边界设置了铁丝网路障。居住在封锁区内的十万居民面临食物供应困难的局面。

据悉，工部局已与日方展开谈判。据工部局警务处总监伯恩少校（Major Bourne）称，12 月 3 日上午举行的旨在立即解除封锁的谈判未取得结果，但制定了一些限制中外居民行动的措施，其性质较为温和。

12 月 3 日，日本士兵、宪兵以及持固定刺刀的中国警察在西区封锁区内巡逻。中国人被禁止出入，也不允许运送食品进入。据说教师和学生将被允许自由通行，但事实证明并非如此。外国人获准通过路障。

封锁区内的大小赌档和商铺均已关闭。该地区米价大幅上涨。

出于对封锁区内中外居民安全的考虑，工部局于 12 月 3 日上午与日方展开谈判，旨在为居民争取通行自由。同时，已请求首席领事与日本总领事展开谈判，以便早日解决此次事端。

首席领事表示，日本总领事对居民处境表示同情，但在当日下午 2 时收到的复信中，日方总领事称，采取这些限制措施是为了便于逮捕凶手，在日本当局认为不可能逮捕到凶手之前，封锁不会解除。

协助谈判的日本警官表示，从日本当局收到的回复来看，封锁在短期内不会解除，甚至有可能持续两至三周。

page_data.en:
December 4, 1940. Afternoon Translation.

According to a person who arrived from
Soochow yesterday, the wrecked train is still on the road-
side and dead bodies are scattered about the place. The
Japanese dead were encoffined on December 1 by coolies sent
by the Central China Railway Company and Soochow Special
Service Organization and were transported to Soochow. Amongst
the more than 120 injured passengers, over 50 seriously
wounded are still in the Soochow Hospital.

P.T.O.

December 4, 1940.
Afternoon Translation

Central China Daily News, Kuo Min Daily News, New China Daily
News and Bing Pao :-

Conditions In The Western District

The Western District area has been blockaded
for four days. The food question in the area is gradually
becoming acute. Yesterday, as a result of a consultation
between the Western District Police and the Japanese, the
food situation was a little better. Yesterday, the Japanese
and the Western District Police decided to issue to residents
in the area temporary passes to enter or leave the area
between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. every day. Those who can procure
shop guarantee can apply for this temporary permission at
the outpost of the Western District Police Bureau, Siao Zar
Kiao (小 不 桥 ). It is learned that yesterday several
thousand people secured such permits. The issuing of permits
will continue for two days. It was temporarily arranged
that people in Zien Ka Hong and Wang Ka Loong will be
allowed to pass. Simultaneously Yu Yuen and Tifeng Roads
were also partly opened. Foreigners are allowed to enter
or leave the area freely.

Chinese-American Daily News (comment) :-

The Blockaded "Happy Land"

The severe blockade of "Happy Land" in the
Shanghai Western District as a result of the shooting of
a Japanese gendarme on Great Western Road entered its fifth
day to-day. Judging by the undermentioned three minor
cases, one can imagine the discomfort and hardship that is
being experienced by the people living inside the blockaded
area :-
(1) A Chinese woman who works in a foreign
family in the French Concession but who lives in the
blockaded area has five children. On ordinary days she
used to return home after her work, but since Saturday last
she has not been able to visit her children. She is wild
with anxiety as there is no food left in the house.
(2) As they were late in leaving school on
Saturday last, six Chinese students, their ages varying
from 6 to 10, have been confined in the premises of the
S.M.C. Public School on Edinburgh Road with five teachers.
They are living on biscuits and sleep on wooden benches,
sharing three or four blankets with their five teachers.
(3) The 85 Chinese and foreign girl telephone
operators at the Lucerne Exchange, who had spent almost 60
hours at their posts since the enforcement of the blockade
and who had had only four hours sleep, were relieved by a
new shift yesterday morning.
Notwithstanding the negotiations opened by
the Consular Body and the S.M.C. with the Japanese
authorities for the lifting of the blockade and that
permission be given for food supplies to be sent into
the blockaded area, the Japanese authorities do not seem
willing to remove the blockade until the culprit is
apprehended. If the Japanese authorities insist on this,

P. T. O.

《华中日报》、《国民日报》、《新中国日报》及《申报》：

西区状况

西区已被封锁四天。该地区的粮食问题正逐渐变得严峻。昨日，经西区警署与日方协商，粮食状况略有好转。昨日，日方与西区警署决定，向该地区居民签发临时通行证，允许其每日上午9时至下午5时进出该地区。凡能取得商铺担保者，可向西区警察局小不桥（Siao Zar Kiao）哨所申请此项临时许可。据悉，昨日有数千人获得了此类许可证。发证工作将持续两天。暂作安排，允许先家洪（Zien Ka Hong）和王家弄（Wang Ka Loong）的居民通行。同时，豫园路（Yu Yuen Road）和提丰路（Tifeng Road）也部分开放。外国人可自由进出该地区。

《中美日报》（评论）：

被封锁的“快乐世界”

由于一名日本宪兵在大西路（Great Western Road）遭枪击，上海西区的“快乐世界”遭到严厉封锁，今日已进入第五天。从下述三起轻微案例中，可以想见生活在封锁区内的人们所经历的困苦与艰难：
(1) 一名在法租界外籍家庭做工但居住在封锁区内的中国妇女，育有五名子女。平日她下班后便回家，但自上周六以来，她一直无法回去看望孩子。她焦虑万分，因为家中已无存粮。
(2) 上周六放学较晚，六名年龄在6至10岁之间的中国学生，连同五名教师，被困在爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）工部局公立学校校内。他们以饼干充饥，睡在长木凳上，与五名教师共用三四条毯子。
(3) 卢塞恩电话交换局（Lucerne Exchange）的85名中外籍女接线员，自封锁实施以来已在岗位上坚守近60小时，仅睡眠四小时，于昨日上午由新一班人员接替。

尽管领事团和工部局已与日本当局展开谈判，要求解除封锁并允许向封锁区内运送粮食，但日本当局似乎不愿在罪犯被捕之前解除封锁。如果日本当局坚持此举，

page_data.en:
December 4, 1940. Afternoon Translation

then it is possible that the blockaded will never be lifted
because, according to information given to the "Shanghai Evening
Post & Mercury" by a certain British resident in the area, the
mercenary policemen guarding the exits are allowing people to
enter or leave upon payment of a dollar or two. Then, is it
not possible for the culprit to have already availed himself
of the opportunity to make good his escape? . Innocent people
are now being made to suffer, particularly those who are poor
and who are unable to pay a dollar to policemen. Starvation
seems to be their fate.
All this reminds us of the blockade of
the Tientsin Concessions last year.
page_data.zh:
1940年12月4日。下午译文

那么，封锁有可能永远不会解除，因为据该地区一名英国居民向《上海晚邮报与信使报》（Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury）提供的消息，守卫出口的雇佣警察正允许人们在支付一两美元后进入或离开。既然如此，罪犯难道不可能已经利用这一机会成功逃脱了吗？无辜者正在遭受苦难，尤其是那些贫穷且无力向警察支付一美元的人。饥饿似乎成了他们的命运。
这一切让我们想起了去年天津租界的封锁。

The situation in the Blockaded Area on the 
Western District Roads remained unchanged on 6/12/40. 

The 3 M/Buses of the Western Shanghai Citizens 
Bus Company comnenced operating on the same Routes 
as the previous day at 7a.m. 6412/40, and no 
additional Buses have been put into operation. 

Foreigners however were refused permission to 
Pass the Barricades at Zast End ot Yu Yuen Road and 
Avenue Haig, even though they stated their intention 
of proceeding by these Buses. 

Police patrols were permitted to proceed west 
on Great Western Road and through the Barricade at 
Great Western - Edinburgh corner but not permitted 
to return through the barricade in the opposite 
direction. . 

Chinese in private m/cars and Silver Taxis 
were permitted freely through this particular 
Barricade after searching, but Foreigners on foot 
or in m/cars were not permitted through this 
barricade. . 

The Barricade on Edinburgh Road neiae Great 
Western Road was opened on 6/12/40 A.Me, permitting 
Foreign and Chinese pedestrians and traffic to pass 
North along Edinburgh Road as far as but net through 
the barricade just south of Yu Yen Road, which 
remained closed. 

Police patrols were permitted to proceed ‘dn 
both directions on Yu Yuen Road via Tifeng Road

and througr the barricades on Yu Yuen Road East of 
Edinburgh Road. 

Chinese in Private m/cars and Silver Taxis were 
permitted freely througi this parricade without search 
but Foreigners in m/cars were not permitted to pass 
although a few Foreigners on foot were permitted to 
pass through occasionally. 

At ll a.m. 6/12/40, three members of S.C.GeP. 
Bureau on a m/cycle visited the Tifeng Road Camp 
and asked C.P.S. 199, who was on duty inside, how 
many police were on duty there and if they were ecmed. 

At about 1 p.m. 6/12/40, two m/cars, one owned by 
the Japanese Military, containing one Japanese Gendarme 
in uniform and about 11 other Chinese or Japanese, all 
carrying Mauser pistols in their hands, stopped at the 
Tifeng Road Camp and demanded that C.P.S. 199 open the 
@oor for them to enter. 

When the C.P.S. replied that he was locked in the 
Camp anc the keys of the gates were at B'Well Station, 
jhe men tried the gate and then drove away in their 
m/car. 

Inspector Yamaguchi made enquiries at 96 Jeasfield 
Road, but was unable to obtain any information regarding 
the reason for this visit to the camp and he was inform 
ed that the men were probably a passing patrol who tried 
to enter and inspect the camp. 

At 1 p.m. 6/12/40, three members of the 3.C.G.P. 
Bureau, one in plain clothes, called at the Publie 


Sehool for Girls on Yu Yuen Road and enquired of the 
C.P.W. on the gate particulars of all watchmen employ= 
ed on the premises. Before leaving, they told the 
CiaF.W. to request the Principal of the school to 
attend a meeting at No. 13 Jessfield Road at 2 pem. 
6/12/40. 

Miss Alexander, Principal of the school, saw the 
man talking to the C.P.W. from the school window and 
subsequently she telephoned fo C/Inspector West, 
reporting the occurrence, and stated she would not 
attend the mecting. 

At 2 pom. 6/12/40, the undersigned and Inspector 
Heu visited 13 Jessfield Road and interviewed Inspector 
Wong Tao Tsun ( ) of the S.C.G.P. Burean who 
stated that on the orders of the &.C.G@.P. Bureau it was 
proposed to remove all watchmen, both Private and 
Police, employed in the barricaded area and replace 
them by watchmen provided by the S.C.G.P. Bureau. 

Fereigners and other employers desirous of retain- 
ing their precent watchman may possibly be permitted 
to do so by the S.C.G.P. Bureau prDvided they furnished 
guarantors and the watchmen wore the uniform ef and 
came under the control of the 3.C.G.P. Buream.. . 

It was explained to Inspector Wong that the 
s’hools and camps were 3.M.C. Property and watchmen 
were provided there by the S.M.P. and P.W.D. : 

He replied that if the S.M.C. has any objections 
they should take the matter up with the 8.C.G@eP. “parean

and Japanese Gendarmerie as soon as possible, as he 
was gathering particulars of all watehmen and 
approaching employers. 

The meeting had been called at 2 p.m. 6/12/40, at 
13 Jessfield Road, for the purpose of informang all 
employers oi watchmen inside the barricaded area of 
the intentions of the S.C.G.P. Bureau. 

At 9 p.m. 5/12/40, a Mr. Ingliss, residing at 596 
Amherst Avenue telephoned the station and reported 
that Mr. T.J. Smith (British), residing 4/2 Tifeng Road 
had been arrested by the S.C.G@. Police at Great Western Rd. 
Edinburgh Roads barricade. 

F.S. 822 telephoned to 94 Jessfield Road and 
ascertained that Mr. Smith had been arrested following 
a slight misunderstanding at the Barricade, 

At 9.20 p.m. 5/12/40 a further telephone message 
was received from Mr. Ingliss reporting Mr. Smith had 
been released and was with him at the house of a 
friend in the French Concession. Mr. Smith, who it 
is believed was under the influence of drink, refused 
to Speak on the piione and stated he would come to 
Bubbling Well Station and report on 6/12/40 AcM. 

At 8.45 a.m. 6/12/40, Mr. Smith came to Bubbling 
Weal Shation and reported that at about 8.30 Pome 
6/12/40, at Edinburgh - Great Western Roads he was 
refused permission to pass the barricade and during an 
altercation which ensued, he struck a 8.C.@. ‘Police 


Constable and was then requested to go to a Police 


Station (unknown) where the affair was settled amicably. 
He did not wish to take the matter any further and 
considered the incident closed, but during the argument, 
at the Barricade, he alleges he lost a siiver wristlet 
watch, oblong shape, on a white cloth strap, value £5. 

He was unable to give a better description of the 
watch, but stated he intended claiming from his 
Insurance Company for the loss. 

House to house searches by the Japanese Gendarmerie 
were continuing throughout the day in the blockaded area 
bordered by Great Western, Edinburgh and Yu Yuen Roads. 

No reports of undue hardships through lack of food, 
etc., were received or noticed in the area and discreet 
enquiries reveal that most of the residents have removed, 
but those remaining in area where Lanes are barricaded 
are assisted in obtaining food supplies and daily 
necessities by members of the S.C.G.P. Bureau, who are 


on duty in vicinity.
